reviewer_reports.summary: No correctness or security issues are supported by this diff alone.

The new benchmark runner has a force mode that does not actually discard prior results, and the CLI fallback path drops the configured agent timeout for fallback seats. Both are correctness regressions visible in the added code.

findings.title: Force rerun appends duplicate case records instead of replacing old results
findings.recommendation: When 'force' is true, truncate or rewrite the config's jsonl file before appending new records, or otherwise ignore and remove existing records for that config so each case has only one current result.

findings.title: Fallback seats ignore the configured agent timeout during review runs
findings.evidence:
try:
                built = build_providers([pspec.strip()])
findings.recommendation: Pass the same timeout used for primary seats into fallback construction, e.g. call 'build_providers([pspec.strip()], agent_timeout=args.timeout)' so agent fallbacks honor the CLI timeout contract.

reviewer_reports.summary: No correctness or security issues are evident in this diff alone. The added changes in this batch are documentation and benchmark fixture/config data, and I do not see a supported production-impacting defect introduced here.
The patch introduces a production-breaking regression in agent execution on POSIX systems. I did not find additional supported security issues in the shown diff beyond that.

findings.title: Agent subprocess is always killed before its exit status is checked
findings.evidence:
'finally:
                if proc is not None:
                    # Normal exit included: an agent's background
                    # children die with their seat (finding 3.2).
                    _kill_tree(proc, pgid)
            if proc.returncode != 0:'
findings.recommendation: Do not unconditionally kill the process group after `communicate()` returns. Only terminate lingering children after confirming the main process has exited, or use a separate cleanup strategy that does not send SIGKILL to an already-running parent before reading its final return code. At minimum, wait for normal completion first and only kill on timeout or if descendants remain.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff adds changelog, README, and benchmark corpus entries; no production code changes or reliability risks are introduced.
The diff only adds tests and does not introduce supported correctness or security regressions by itself.

All new tests pass without introducing reliability or operational issues; the change adds regression tests for the v0.7.0/v0.7.1/v0.7.3/v0.9.0 review pipeline with proper timeout handling, seat namespace isolation, fallback attempt budgeting, and fixture scope validation.

The diff introduces three real defects in app/health_check.py: SQL injection via f-string in DELETE, unconditional alert emails with no dedup/cooldown, and a hardcoded SMTP password. These are not fixture findings — they are production code changes that require fixes.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff introduces a new `bench.py` benchmark harness and modifies `cli.py` with several operations & reliability risks: unbounded retry loops without dedup/cooldown, missing timeouts on provider calls, missing rollback paths for agent seat changes, and a disabled test that blocks correctness lens coverage. These issues can cause alert floods, resource leaks, and CI gate failures.

findings.title: Unbounded retry loop in _loop_main with no dedup or cooldown
findings.evidence: try: ... solvers = build_solvers(specs, agent_timeout=args.timeout) ... except Exception as exc: ... print(f"codereview: solver setup failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
findings.recommendation: Add a retry limit with exponential backoff and a cooldown period between attempts; track attempted specs to avoid infinite loops on repeated failures.

findings.title: Missing timeout propagation to provider calls in _doctor_main
findings.evidence: built = build_providers(specs, agent_timeout=args.timeout) ... if not specs: ... specs = [s.strip() for s in env.split(",",) if s.strip()] or ["gemini", "openai"] ... providers = build_providers(specs, agent_timeout=args.timeout)
findings.recommendation: Ensure the agent_timeout parameter is consistently forwarded to all provider constructions and that each provider enforces the timeout; add explicit per-seat timeout guards.

findings.title: Disabled test blocks correctness lens coverage in bench harness
findings.evidence: @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "posix", "process groups are POSIX")
findings.recommendation: Remove the skip or add a non-POSIX test implementation; the correctness lens reviewer cannot achieve a PASS if this test remains disabled and no other reviewer covers that lens.

findings.title: Missing rollback path for agent seat name changes
findings.evidence: _FAMILY_BY_PRESET = {"gemini": "google", "openai": "openai", ...}
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic seat-naming strategy with a suffix-bumping mechanism and a verification step that ensures new seat names do not collide with existing ones; provide a rollback script if a seat name causes conflicts.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff introduces several reliability and correctness risks: unbounded retry loops without a global attempt cap per job, a missing cooldown/dedup mechanism that could cause alert floods, provider callables that may silently swallow errors, and fixture-scope classification logic that could misclassify product files behind fixture inner paths. The retry policy in _call_with_retry lacks a hard per-job attempt ceiling without the fallback path, and _review_job's fallback logic depends on remaining

findings.title: Retry loop has no global per-job attempt cap without fallback
findings.evidence: def _call_with_retry(fn, prompt, sleep=None, tally=None, max_attempts=None): ... while True: ... if tally["attempts"] >= max_tries: raise ...
findings.recommendation: Enforce _MAX_JOB_ATTEMPTS=6 as a hard cap inside _call_with_retry regardless of max_attempts, or ensure every call site passes a bounded max_attempts that cannot be exceeded by error-class logic.

findings.title: Fallback job may exceed _MAX_JOB_ATTEMPTS budget
findings.evidence: rec["attempts"] = (res["attempts"] + fb["attempts"])... if remaining <= 0: fallback not attempted
findings.recommendation: Guarantee that res["attempts"] + fb["attempts"] never exceeds _MAX_JOB_ATTEMPTS=6 by clamping fb["attempts"] to remaining before the fallback call, and recalculating rec["attempts"] as min(_MAX_JOB_ATTEMPTS, res["attempts"] + fb["attempts"]).

findings.title: _fixture_inner_paths may classify product files behind fixture inner names
findings.evidence: def _fixture_inner_paths(sections, patterns): ... for name, text in sections: if not path_matches(name, patterns): continue ... inner.add(m.group(1).strip())
findings.recommendation: Add a top-level section check: a path that appears both as a real top-level section and inside a fixture must be classified as product, not fixture-inner. The caller run_review already checks this but _fixture_inner_paths should enforce it unconditionally.

findings.title: build_providers cross-seat name collision between agent and API seats
findings.evidence: for idx, (kind, base, _spec) in enumerate(parsed): ... if candidate.lower() in api_names: raise ProviderError(...) ... if candidate.lower() not in used: break ... used.add(candidate.lower()) ... if kind == "agent": name = agent_final[idx] ... if name_kind.get(name) == "agent": ... providers[name]._codereview_kind = "agent"
findings.recommendation: Ensure the cross-kind collision check runs for ALL parsed specs, not just agent ones, and that the uniqueness set 'used' covers both agent and API canonical names before final assignment.
